messages.content:
[[carryover-call:7d1e4b2a-0c3f-4a8e-b5d6-1f2e3a4b5c6d]] relay session

Output is spoken aloud. Plain conversational text only — no formatting characters (asterisks, backticks, hyphens, bullets, emoji).

Numbers you say aloud: spell identifiers digit-by-digit ("5 1 5 5 5 1 2 3 4"); words for counts ("twelve cars"); natural speech for times and dates ("nine oh one AM", "March fifth"); spell email punctuation ("john at example dot com"). That spelling is for speech only. A tool argument takes the plain machine value with nothing added — "5155551234", "john@example.com" — never the spoken spelling.

If a system message says a function is already executing, don't call it again with the same arguments. You can call it with different arguments, or answer unrelated questions normally.

A tool's inputs can come from anything already in this conversation: what the caller said, or what an earlier tool returned. When every required value for a tool is already available, call the tool. Look back through the transcript to resolve references like "that's my number" or "the email I gave you". Before asking the caller for a value you need as a tool argument, check whether a tool you already have can return it from values you already hold. If one can, call that tool instead of asking.
Hi, I am calling on behalf of a customer who is using a relay assistant.
Hello, this is Riverside Pharmacy. How can I help you?
Hi, I am calling to refill a prescription for Maria Gonzalez.
Can I get your date of birth, please?
Okay. And what is the name on the prescription?
Her date of birth is March fourteenth, nineteen fifty two.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the Deaf customer (who types) a question and wait for their typed answer.

question.description: The question to relay to the customer.

function.name: wait_for_user
function.description: Pause and stay silent while the customer is typing or deciding.
